finalFiles.CONTRACT.md:
# Accepted invoice behavior

Implement export function invoiceTotals(invoices) in invoices.mjs. The input is an array of invoice objects. Every invoice has status paid or unpaid and a nonnegative integer amountCents. Reject non-arrays, unknown statuses, negative amounts, and fractional amounts, including malformed unpaid invoices, with an Error. For valid input, return exactly {count, totalCents}, counting and summing paid invoices only. Empty input returns zeros. Preserve input objects and arrays.

INV-001 covers valid totals, empty and unpaid-only inputs, zero values, and input preservation. INV-002 covers rejected inputs. No currency conversion, scheduler, UI, or external integration is part of this delivery.

# Invoice helper

`invoiceTotals(invoices)` validates invoices and summarizes paid amounts in integer cents.

```js
import { invoiceTotals } from './invoices.mjs';

invoiceTotals([
  { status: 'paid', amountCents: 1250 },
  { status: 'unpaid', amountCents: 9999 },
  { status: 'paid', amountCents: 75 },
]); // { count: 2, totalCents: 1325 }
```

The result has exactly `count` and `totalCents`. Empty and unpaid-only arrays return zeros; paid invoices with zero amounts still count. Inputs are preserved. Every invoice must have status `paid` or `unpaid` and a nonnegative integer `amountCents`. Non-arrays and malformed entries throw an Error, including malformed unpaid invoices.

Run `node --test invoices.test.mjs` using the existing Node installation. No additional dependencies are needed. See the [accepted contract](CONTRACT.md), [project documentation](docs/README.md), and [delivery plan](docs/plans/delivery.md). No currency conversion, scheduling, UI, or external integration is included. Exact arithmetic beyond JavaScript Number precision is not specified or verified.

# Integer amounts

The candidate convention to keep amounts in integer cents is confirmed for this invoice delivery by [the accepted contract](../../CONTRACT.md). Validate amounts before filtering by paid status: ignoring unpaid invoices first would admit malformed amounts. A controlled fault that skipped unpaid validation made the `unpaid-fractional` test fail because no Error was thrown; the intended implementation passes the paid/unpaid amount matrix. See [verification notes](../testing/invoice-totals.md) and the assertions in invoices.test.mjs.

Use this guidance for invoice totals only. It does not establish a general money representation policy, currency conversion behavior, or safe arithmetic beyond JavaScript Number precision. Recheck the current contract before reuse; the note remains subordinate to it.

# Invoice totals verification

`node --test invoices.test.mjs` passed 39 Unit tests after implementation and again after controlled-fault experiments. INV-001 covers exact mixed paid totals, unpaid-only and empty input, paid zero values, fresh result objects, and preservation of caller metadata and frozen inputs. INV-002 covers non-arrays, malformed entries, unknown statuses, missing fields, and negative, fractional, nonnumeric, and nonfinite amounts for both paid and unpaid entries. Invalid entries follow a valid paid entry to exercise validation after accumulation.

Two isolated copies under ignored `.trial-output/` tested assertion effectiveness without modifying production code. Replacing amount accumulation with `totalCents += 1` made `mixed-totals` fail with actual 2 versus expected 1325. Skipping unpaid entries before validation made `unpaid-fractional` fail with a missing expected Error. Each targeted runner exited 1 with ERR_ASSERTION; only these assertions receive controlled-fault credit. The intended implementation then passed all 39 tests.

Against the initial Git baseline, no implementation or tests existed. Both accepted criteria and their IDs remain active. All new tests are retained; no assertion or criterion is retired. Coverage, effectiveness, and lifecycle policies remain at their inherited review defaults, independently of enabled execution evidence. Scoped review records capture inspected input hashes. # Design

## Context

This package is a library. [The accepted contract](../../../../CONTRACT.md) defines the complete delivery boundary; [the delivery plan](../../../../docs/plans/delivery.md) holds future work.

## Approach and Alternatives

Use a single pass over the array. Before counting an entry, validate that it is an object with status `paid` or `unpaid` and a nonnegative integer `amountCents`. Validate unpaid entries too. Accumulate only paid entries and return a fresh object with exactly `count` and `totalCents`. Read caller data without sorting, annotating, or rewriting it.

Filtering unpaid entries before validation would silently accept malformed invoices and violates the contract. Currency conversion, scheduler design, and UI design are excluded. Use JavaScript Number arithmetic; the contract does not define overflow handling or exact sums beyond Number precision, so do not add a safe-integer rejection requirement.

## Durable Decisions

No new Decision Record is needed for this simple contract-defined module.

## Risks and Verification

The main risk is skipping validation on unpaid entries. Unit tests cross each invalid amount with both statuses and place malformed unpaid entries after valid paid ones. INV-001 tests mixed input, exact result shape, empty/unpaid-only input, paid zero, and deep input preservation including caller metadata and frozen objects. INV-002 tests non-arrays, unknown statuses, missing fields, malformed entries, negatives, fractions, and nonnumeric/nonfinite values. Assertions compare concrete expected totals or require an Error. Controlled faults will test whether those assertions detect incorrect paid totals and bypassed unpaid validation. Inputs with getters/proxies and numerical overflow are outside the verified boundary.

# Proposal

## Why
Maintainers need paid invoice totals in integer cents, as accepted in [the invoice contract](../../../../CONTRACT.md). This is new library behavior, so the existing OpenSpec change remains appropriate after narrowing.

## What Changes
- Export `invoiceTotals(invoices)` from `invoices.mjs`.
- Validate every invoice, including unpaid entries, and return exactly `{count, totalCents}` for paid entries without mutation.
- Keep scheduling and appearance out of this delivery. Their purpose, dependencies, and reassessment remain in the [sole delivery backlog](../../../../docs/plans/delivery.md).

## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
- invoices: calculate and validate paid invoice totals

### Modified Capabilities
None.

## Impact
One dependency-free library module and Node unit tests, using only INV-001 and INV-002. Update README usage, the documentation index, the existing integer-amounts lesson, and the delivery plan. CONTRACT.md, enabled policies, and ID reservations remain unchanged.

## Scope assessment

The original bundle assumes that a library needs scheduled delivery and a visual interface. The supplied fixture feedback contradicts that assumption. A credible alternative is an invoice-only module with later scheduling designed around an identified channel. Reading the contract and local plan is the cheapest useful investigation and supports that alternative. Revisit scope only when a channel or UI product is selected; no such approval is present. Even passing the two invoice criteria would not deliver automatic summaries or a UI; those are separate outcomes, preserved in the backlog. The user's trial instruction authorizes this invoice behavior, local commits, and archive after verification, without approving either deferred feature.

## Purpose
Provide validated paid invoice totals for library consumers.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Valid totals
The library SHALL export `invoiceTotals(invoices)` from `invoices.mjs`. For an array of valid invoice objects it SHALL return exactly `{count, totalCents}`, counting and summing only entries whose status is `paid`, without changing the input array or objects.

#### Scenario: Valid totals [INV-001]
Test-type: Unit
- **WHEN** invoices with `paid` or `unpaid` status and nonnegative integer `amountCents` are supplied
- **THEN** only paid invoices contribute to count and total cents, including paid zero amounts
- **AND** empty and unpaid-only inputs return `{count: 0, totalCents: 0}`
- **AND** the input array, objects, and caller metadata remain unchanged

### Requirement: Reject invalid inputs
The library SHALL throw an Error for non-array input or any malformed invoice, including unpaid invoices. Every invoice SHALL have status `paid` or `unpaid` and a nonnegative integer `amountCents`; unknown statuses, missing fields, negative amounts, and fractional amounts SHALL be rejected.

#### Scenario: Invalid invoices [INV-002]
Test-type: Unit
- **WHEN** malformed invoice input is supplied
- **THEN** it throws an Error

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 Implement invoiceTotals and Unit tests in invoices.test.mjs for INV-001 and INV-002: exact paid totals, empty/unpaid/zero boundaries, preservation, and rejection including malformed unpaid entries. Run `node --test invoices.test.mjs`; complete only after all cases pass and README usage matches.

## 2. Final verification

- [x] 2.1 Review assertions with controlled total and unpaid-validation faults, restore behavior, and run `node --test invoices.test.mjs`. Maintain affected docs, learning, backlog, scoped quality review, and local links; validate with `openspec validate add-invoice-tools --strict`. Complete only with actual results recorded and no unresolved behavior failures.

Results: 39/39 Unit tests passed; both targeted controlled faults produced ERR_ASSERTION and exit 1 in isolated copies; intended behavior passed again. Strict change validation, the README example, and 17 local Markdown links passed. See [verification notes](../../../../docs/testing/invoice-totals.md). Fault effectiveness is established only for mixed-totals and unpaid-fractional; remaining cases have reviewed assertions but no controlled-fault outcome, so policy review warnings remain to disclose.

## Workflow follow-up

Commit reviewed inputs, collect change-scoped execution evidence, and run Cliewen check on clean HEAD. Archive using native OpenSpec after verification under the user's existing authorization. Repair moved links, reassess the sole backlog, refresh permanent-spec review, commit all closure edits, then recollect evidence without --change and check permanent specs on the final clean revision. Archive and evidence collection are untracked follow-ups, not implementation checkboxes.
